sets.title: Authorization decision: ORM-style data access vs SQL-oriented vs rule re-expression
sets.description: The same resource-authorization decision in three semantically equivalent forms: carrier A uses the pristine access_guard with direct array access, carrier B applies ORM-style repository pattern with simulated data-access methods (sem_orm_sql variant), and carrier C re-expresses authorization using compound rule predicates with different condition grouping (sem_rule variant). All three compute behaviorally identical results. No two carriers share a token run long enough for token/line tools to pair them, so only semantic detection is expected to recover the cluster.
sets.notes: SEM-07 variant (sem_orm_sql) uses ORM-style inline repository logic. SEM-01 variant (sem_rule) uses rule re-expression with compound predicates. Behavioral equivalence enforced by gen/seeds/access_guard/equivalence_test.php.

distractors.reason: near-miss: same auth vocabulary (user/resource/roles/grants/status) but computes a numeric trust score, not a boolean decision
